questions.prompt: Two lines cross. One angle is 72°. What is the vertically opposite angle?
Two angles form a linear pair (a straight line). One is 125°. Find the other.
Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 70°. What is the corresponding angle?
questions.explain: Corresponding angles are equal when lines are parallel.

questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One co-interior angle is 118°. Find the other.
A transversal (not perpendicular) crosses two parallel lines, making 8 angles. How many different angle sizes are there?
questions.explain: Every angle is either θ or 180° − θ.

questions.prompt: Two angles are complementary. One is 35°. Find the other.
Explain how you could use a transversal and a protractor to check whether two lines painted on a playground are parallel.
questions.modelAnswer: Draw (or imagine) a straight line crossing both painted lines. Measure a pair of corresponding (or alternate) angles with a protractor. If they are equal, the lines are parallel; if they are different, the lines are not parallel. (Or check that co-interior angles add to 180°.)
rubric: States the condition for parallel lines
questions.explain: Criterion C: explain a method clearly.

questions.prompt: When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, alternate interior angles are…
questions.explain: They form a Z shape and are equal.
